scenes.img: In a tribal village, Shabari: young tribal woman, dark skin, black hair in a bun, a simple brown-ochre sari, bead necklaces turns away from a wedding feast where animals are being prepared, sad, choosing to leave.
scenes.text: The story goes that long ago, a young tribal woman named Shabari left her home… because she could not bear to see animals killed for her wedding feast.

scenes.img: Shabari: young tribal woman, dark skin, black hair in a bun, a simple brown-ochre sari, bead necklaces kneels with folded hands at the entrance of a forest hermitage before the old sage Matanga, who has a long white beard and a saffron robe.
scenes.text: She walked into the forest, to the hermitage of the sage Matanga… and asked to serve.

scenes.img: Shabari: young tribal woman, dark skin, black hair in a bun, a simple brown-ochre sari, bead necklaces quietly sweeps a forest path with a broom and carries water in a clay pot, in a peaceful hermitage among trees.
scenes.text: She swept the paths. She fetched water. She did every small task, quietly… for years.

scenes.img: The very old sage Matanga, lying on a mat near the end of his life, holds the hand of Shabari: young tribal woman, dark skin, black hair in a bun, a simple brown-ochre sari, bead necklaces and speaks to her, pointing toward the forest path.
scenes.text: When the old sage was dying, he told her: one day, Rama himself will come to this place. Wait for him.

scenes.img: Shabari: young tribal woman, dark skin, black hair in a bun, a simple brown-ochre sari, bead necklaces sits alone at the door of a small hut in the forest, looking down the empty path, the evening light fading.
At dawn, Shabari: young tribal woman, dark skin, black hair in a bun, a simple brown-ochre sari, bead necklaces sweeps the forest path and scatters fresh flowers along it, smiling softly.
scenes.text: Every morning she swept the path he might walk on… and scattered fresh flowers on it.

scenes.img: In the forest, Shabari: young tribal woman, dark skin, black hair in a bun, a simple brown-ochre sari, bead necklaces picks wild berries from a bush and tastes one carefully, putting only the sweet ones into a small leaf bowl.
scenes.text: Every day she gathered berries for him… and tasted each one, so that she would only offer him the sweet ones.

scenes.img: Shabari: the same tribal woman grown very old, dark wrinkled skin, white hair in a bun, bent back, a simple brown-ochre sari, bead necklaces, kind eyes sits at the door of her small forest hut, still watching the path, fresh flowers on the ground, autumn leaves falling.
scenes.text: Days became years. Years became decades. Her hair turned white. Her back bent. Still… she waited.

scenes.img: Two passing young men point and laugh at Shabari: the same tribal woman grown very old, dark wrinkled skin, white hair in a bun, bent back, a simple brown-ochre sari, bead necklaces, kind eyes, who sweeps the forest path anyway, calm and patient.
scenes.text: Some people laughed at her. A prince… coming here? To an old woman’s hut?

scenes.img: Down the flower-strewn forest path walk two young men in forest clothes with bows: Rama: blue-skinned young prince, clean-shaven, long hair tied up, a bow on his shoulder, simple forest clothes of bark-coloured cloth; Lakshmana: fair-skinned young prince, clean-shaven, hair tied up, a bow, simple forest clothes. In the foreground, Shabari: the same tribal woman grown very old, dark wrinkled skin, white hair in a bun, bent back, a simple brown-ochre sari, bead necklaces, kind eyes stands up in wonder.
scenes.text: And then one day… two young men walked down the path. Rama… and his brother Lakshmana.

scenes.img: Shabari: the same tribal woman grown very old, dark wrinkled skin, white hair in a bun, bent back, a simple brown-ochre sari, bead necklaces, kind eyes kneels and touches the feet of Rama: blue-skinned young prince, clean-shaven, long hair tied up, a bow on his shoulder, simple forest clothes of bark-coloured cloth, weeping with joy, while Rama bends down to lift her; Lakshmana stands behind.
scenes.text: Shabari fell at Rama’s feet, weeping. She had waited her whole life… for this moment.

scenes.img: Shabari: the same tribal woman grown very old, dark wrinkled skin, white hair in a bun, bent back, a simple brown-ochre sari, bead necklaces, kind eyes holds out a small leaf bowl of wild berries to Rama: blue-skinned young prince, clean-shaven, long hair tied up, a bow on his shoulder, simple forest clothes of bark-coloured cloth, her hands trembling, worried and shy.
scenes.text: She offered him her berries, the ones she had tasted… and suddenly she was afraid. Were they good enough?

scenes.img: Rama: blue-skinned young prince, clean-shaven, long hair tied up, a bow on his shoulder, simple forest clothes of bark-coloured cloth sits on a simple mat outside the hut eating berries from the leaf bowl with a warm smile, while Shabari: the same tribal woman grown very old, dark wrinkled skin, white hair in a bun, bent back, a simple brown-ochre sari, bead necklaces, kind eyes watches with tears of joy and Lakshmana: fair-skinned young prince, clean-shaven, hair tied up, a bow, simple forest clothes looks on.
scenes.text: Rama ate them all, with joy. He said he had never tasted anything sweeter… because they were offered with love.

scenes.img: Shabari: the same tribal woman grown very old, dark wrinkled skin, white hair in a bun, bent back, a simple brown-ochre sari, bead necklaces, kind eyes points into the distance toward far mountains, guiding Rama: blue-skinned young prince, clean-shaven, long hair tied up, a bow on his shoulder, simple forest clothes of bark-coloured cloth and Lakshmana: fair-skinned young prince, clean-shaven, hair tied up, a bow, simple forest clothes, who listen carefully.
scenes.text: Then Shabari told Rama the way to Sugriva and Hanuman… the path that would lead him to Sita.

scenes.img: Shabari: the same tribal woman grown very old, dark wrinkled skin, white hair in a bun, bent back, a simple brown-ochre sari, bead necklaces, kind eyes sits peacefully with folded hands before a small sacred fire at dusk, glowing with calm, as Rama: blue-skinned young prince, clean-shaven, long hair tied up, a bow on his shoulder, simple forest clothes of bark-coloured cloth raises his hand in blessing.
scenes.text: And her waiting was complete. The story goes that she entered the sacred fire… and rose to the highest heaven.
Shabari had no wealth, no learning, no family name. Only her love… and her patience.
Krishna says in the Gita… Fix your mind on me, love me… and you will come to me. I promise you truly. For you are dear to me.
